correctness.rationale: The normalized Dieterich state equation with constant normal stress integrates exactly to the positive kernel \(D(t)=1+a^{-1}\int_0^t e^{u/a+s(u)}\,du\); cumulative expected events equal \(ra\log D(t)\). Maximization of the weighted exponential functional uses a strict endpoint chord and strictly increasing bathtub rearrangement; minimizing it uses strict pointwise convexity and the unique budget-compatible clamped affine profile. Integration of the three pieces reproduces both claimed count bounds, including all boundary plateau cases. Exact ODE composition and kernel quadrature agree on 600 randomized feasible protocols; the analytic inequalities, not finite checks, establish the universal result.

originality.rationale: The original model and arbitrary-stress integral are explicitly acknowledged; the independently derived novel content is a sharp all-history fixed-stress-exposure variational characterization with a late bang-bang maximizer, clipped affine minimizer, exact budget multiplier equation, and unique extremizers. Full-text checks of the closest model and injection-optimization papers do not state or subsume that conclusion. Residual risks of inaccessible 1994 full text and generic convex-allocation aliases remain disclosed, so this is a self-review, not an independent novelty certification.
residual_risks: Dieterich 1994 full text inaccessible after bounded attempts, so a mathematically equivalent passage there cannot be completely excluded.
An exact box- and integral-constrained optimizer of weighted exponentials could appear under generic convex optimization or load-shaping vocabulary and would dominate after reduction.
Literature and research-record searches are finite and not proof of universal novelty.

The stress-time budget is a modeling assumption, not equivalent to real reservoir flow or injection-volume constraints; 2022 and 2026 operational-control literature addresses a different feasible set.
Results concern expected event counts of a homogeneous constitutive model; they do not certify empirical earthquake-risk reduction.

value.rationale: The exact envelopes are a motivated finite-horizon stress-response question in seismicity forecasting: equal maximum stress and equal stress-time exposure do not determine the number of expected earthquake nucleations. The theorem gives unique worst and best temporal profiles and closed event-count bounds, replacing an uncontrolled schedule search by an analytic characterization. At \(a=r=1\), \(T=2\), \(H=1.5\), and \(B=2\), expected counts span approximately 2.76977 to 3.27086 compared with baseline 2, a nonnegligible difference even at identical stress exposure. This is a physical-model mathematical envelope, not a field-ready operational design.
